21.text: Chukchee, not even with those of the Tungus, but only with the methods of

22.text: the hungry Russian creoles in getting food for themselves.

23.text: Marriage between Relatives. — The Chukchee have several methods of

24.text: securing brides and concluding marriages. One of these is through marriage

25.text: between relatives, if possible in the same family, or at least in the same camp,

26.text: or in the neighboring camp, where families of the same blood reside. Most

27.text: frequent are marriages between cousins.¹ Marriage between uncle and niece

28.text: is considered incestuous, though I know of one case of an uncle living with

29.text: his niece in clandestine love, and another one of an uncle married to his niece

30.text: according to the customary ritual. He was ridiculed by his neighbors, howe-

31.text: ver, on account of this marriage. Two cases of incestuous intercourse between

32.text: father and daughter are also known to me. Marriage or love between brother

33.text: and sister are also considered as incestuous. Still, in several tales “from the

34.text: time of the first creation” (tot-tɵmg̣aˊt-taˊg̣nêpŭ), i. e., dealing with the creation

35.text: of the world and of mankind, cases of marriage between brother and sister

36.text: are described with more or less detail. Thus, in one tale the first human

37.text: couple are said to have, first a son, then a daughter. The children sit near

38.text: the entrance of the tent, and grow up. The mother does not nurse them.

39.text: They grow up all by themselves. Then the brother marries the sister. They
